newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end with pared gains after limit bulge.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end with pared gains after limit bulge.

text.p: CME November lumber futures ran up for a limit gain of $10.00 per tbf around midsession but prices slipped to close with pared gains.
November posted a limit gain at $352.20 per tbf but closed at $349.80, up $7.60 per tbf. January ended up $6.20 at $360.70 and other months finished $6.70 to $3.90 higher.

Lumber continued its erratic trade of the past few sessions and posted gains from the start despite closing sharply lower Tuesday. The market appears to be consolidating on the charts and will likely trade between $340 to $360, basis November, traders said.
Gains in futures also came despite the continued seasonal setback in cash prices.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $392 per tbf, down $18 from Friday and $38 lower than last week. Expectations are for cash lumber prices to decline to the $350 to $375 area before finding renewed retail and dealer demand, cash sources said.
